article.headline: Bryce Young throws for 2 TDs and leads Panthers to 25-14 win over injury-riddled Eagles
article.description: — Bryce Young hit Tommy Tremble for a touchdown and Carolina's tight end went into full Rocky Balboa mode.
article.linkText: Bryce Young throws for 2 TDs and leads Panthers to 25-14 win over injury-riddled Eagles

images.name: Tommy Tremble pads Panthers' lead with second TD of the day
images.caption: Tommy Tremble pads Panthers' lead with second TD of the day

article.story: PHILADELPHIA -- — Bryce Young hit Tommy Tremble for a touchdown and Carolina's tight end went into full Rocky Balboa mode. Tremble feigned two rights and then delivered an uppercut with his left hand for a pantomime knockout of a Panthers teammate in an end-zone celebration. The once-mighty Philadelphia Eagles — two seasons removed from a Super Bowl championship — have suddenly turned into an NFL punching bag. Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns to Tremble, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score to lead the Panthers past the injury-riddled Eagles 25-14 on Sunday. Tremble did everything but run the Rocky steps. “Great fight in the guys,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. The Panthers (3-2) had little trouble in the second half picking apart the Eagles (2-4), who have lost four straight games for the first time since 2020 and were missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley. Hurts is on injured reserve and will miss at least four games with a blood clot in his calf. Barkley missed his second straight game with a hamstring injury and Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby, his two backups, were also sidelined by injuries. The quarterback showdown between Young and Eagles backup Tanner McKee seemed like a mismatch entering the day. McKee, in his fourth season, made his third career start and first one without the Eagles having already clinched a playoff berth. McKee was sacked for an 11-yard loss on the Eagles’ first play from scrimmage and he nearly had a pass intercepted on second down. The 26-year-old’s outing never got much better, and he finished 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown. He hit DeVonta Smith — who missed the last two games with a hamstring injury — for a 19-yard TD that pulled the Eagles within 19-14 early in the fourth quarter. The Eagles forced a three-and-out and then wasted their drive when McKee lost 12 yards on a fumble. It was one of several examples of miscommunication affecting the offense. “Whether it was guys in the wrong spot, I’ve got to get them fixed or a missed call, I’ve got to get it fixed,” McKee said. Young was happy to take advantage of the Eagles' miscues. He sealed the win with his second TD pass to Tremble, a 19-yarder for a 25-14 lead. Young even heard “MVP!” chants for a small group of Panthers fans there were about the only ones left inside the stadium at the end. “All the Panthers fans being able to be out here all the way in Philly and feeling the support,” Young said. “We all show that. We all feed off of that. Whether it’s here or there, the support for all of us is huge.” Young — who threw a 12-yard TD pass to Tremble in the second quarter — bailed out the Panthers late in the third on third-and-8 at their own 10 when he connected with Jalen Coker for a 32-yard gain. Young extended the drive with a 15-yard completion, and the Panthers converted a fourth-and-1 when Hubbard found a hole for a 19-yard run. Hubbard finished the drive in the fourth with a 2-yard touchdown run for a 19-7 lead. Carolina’s 2-point attempt failed. A week after the Eagles lost by a field goal on the final play against Jacksonville in London, Ryan Fitzgerald made kicks of 47 and 52 yards for the Panthers. The latter made it 13-7 and was his 11th straight successful attempt to open the season. He did miss an extra point. The Eagles are in a world of hurt without Hurts and were forced to turn to McKee, who had lost his grip on the No. 2 spot in training camp. He regained the backup job after the Eagles cut Andy Dalton, but he looked out of place all game. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion did him no favors by calling a series of failed screen and swing passes. McKee threw a third-and-14 sideline pass for Smith in the third quarter that sailed out of bounds against one of the worst defenses in the NFL and was greeted by boos. The struggling offense isn’t all on McKee. The Eagles were shut out in the third quarter and have scored only six points in that quarter all season. Philadelphia had only 37 total yards in the first quarter and punted on its first five drives. Dameon Pierce scored on a 2-yard run to cut Carolina’s lead to 10-7 at halftime.
